g.text: Figure 8d | Training-ranked neurons retain phase-decoding performance efficiently

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #56616f

g.text: All four regions share one accuracy scale; dotted lines are full-cohort performance and dashed lines are 90% of full.

text.style: font-size: 6.7px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #4f5964

g.text: Within every complete-trial training fold, neurons are ranked from decoder coefficient norms. Random-k, top-k and bottom-k decoders are retrained at every retained fraction; the full-cohort training-selected regularization is

text.style: font-size: 6.7px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #4f5964

g.text: reused across subset sizes. n90 is the smallest neuron count reaching 90% of full performance. Efficient prediction does not imply that top-ranked neurons are causally necessary.
